question.problem:
The brightness (in nits) of a certain laptop screen model is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ nits and a standard deviation of $12$ nits. In addition, in $90%$ of cases the brightness is between $0.80\mu $ and $1.20\mu .$ Find the average brightness, **rounding your answer to two decimal places**.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |

$\mu ≈$
{{field-1}}
$nits$
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent screen brightness (in nits). Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{12}^{2}),$ and we want to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.80\mu <X<1.20\mu )=0.90.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.80\mu <X<1.20\mu ) & =0.90 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.20\mu ) & =0.90 \\ P(\mu <X<1.20\mu ) & =0.45 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.20\mu ) & =0.5+0.45 \\ P(X<1.20\mu ) & =0.95.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.20\mu ) & =0.95 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.20\mu }{12}) & =0.95 \\ Φ(\frac{0.20\mu }{12}) & =0.95 \\ \frac{0.20\mu }{12} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.95).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.95)=1.6449.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.20\mu }{12} & =1.6449 \\ 0.20\mu  & =19.7388 \\ \mu  & =\frac{19.7388}{0.20} \\  & ≈98.69\,\text{nits}.\end{aligned}
$$
